title: Justice Bell (Women's Liberty Bell)
status_note: On permanent display at the chapel (inside Valley Forge NHP's boundary but not part of the park).

place.label: Washington Memorial Chapel, Valley Forge, Pennsylvania

maker: Meneely Bell Foundry, Troy, New York

timeline.event: Commissioned by suffragist Katharine Wentworth Ruschenberger and cast at Meneely, Troy (Library of Congress photo of the casting)
Tours all 67 Pennsylvania counties, about 5,000 miles, with its clapper chained silent
Pennsylvania's statewide suffrage referendum fails; the bell stays silent
Tours several states for ratification of the 19th Amendment
Unchained and rung on Independence Square, 48 times, once per state

tiers.everyday: The Justice Bell is a copy of the Liberty Bell made in 1915 for the fight for women's votes. Its clapper was chained so it could not ring until women won the vote in 1920.
tiers.student: NPS: commissioned in 1915 by Katharine Wentworth Ruschenberger of the Pennsylvania Woman Suffrage Association, cast by Meneely in Troy without a crack, inscribed 'ESTABLISH JUSTICE'. It toured Pennsylvania's 67 counties silent; after the 19th Amendment it was rung on 25 September 1920. A Library of Congress photo shows the casting.
